model_rule: Preserve determinism for DAG discovery, --select, spawned children, resume, retries, locks, and cleanup

findings.gap: computeFingerprint hashes raw TASK.md file content (readFileSync) instead of normalized task definition fields. Comments, trailing whitespace, and markdown formatting that don't affect task behavior can change the fingerprint, causing false cache invalidation.
findings.evidence: helpers.ts line 77: readFileSync(taskPath, 'utf-8') reads raw file verbatim, bypassing hashTaskBody (which strips trailing whitespace) and hashTaskFrontmatter (which uses sorted keys via stableStringify)
findings.correction: Make computeFingerprint use hashTaskFrontmatter + hashTaskBody + hashTaskChecks from hash/task.ts instead of raw file content
findings.test_to_write: tests/fingerprint-determinism.test.ts — verify that cosmetic TASK.md edits (comments, trailing whitespace) do not change the fingerprint

findings.gap: computeFingerprint uses JSON.stringify for checks (key order depends on insertion order), while hashTaskChecks uses stableStringify (sorted keys). If check objects are constructed with different key order, fingerprints diverge for semantically identical checks.
findings.evidence: helpers.ts line 91: JSON.stringify(node.taskDef.checks ?? []) — no key sorting. hash/task.ts line 41: stableStringify(checks) — sorts keys.
findings.correction: Replace JSON.stringify with stableStringify in computeFingerprint, or delegate to hashTaskChecks
findings.test_to_write: tests/fingerprint-determinism.test.ts — verify fingerprint is identical when checks objects have different key insertion order

findings.gap: computeFingerprint has two code paths (file exists vs. doesn't) that produce different fingerprints for the same logical task. If file path resolution changes between runs, the fingerprint changes even though the task definition is identical.
findings.evidence: helpers.ts lines 76-78: if (taskPath && existsSync(taskPath)) { hash.update(readFileSync(...)) } else { /* hash taskDef fields */ } — these two paths produce different hashes for the same task
findings.correction: Always hash from the normalized taskDef fields, regardless of whether the source file exists on disk
findings.test_to_write: tests/fingerprint-determinism.test.ts — verify fingerprint is identical whether sourced from file path or taskDef fields
